commits.summary: Example 286's someMap mismatch path runs through the message codes: LinkedHashSet and StringJoiner models on request, String.lastIndexOf(int) and Class.isArray() of a class literal
commits.body:
The state stream's step 3 continued. Binding "32" to someMap records a binding error, and DefaultMessageCodesResolver.resolveMessageCodes now runs to its end in the own checker. Two models on request: java.util.LinkedHashSet (the HashSet model with its elements in the order first added: add, toArray(), toArray(T[]); asking for it also runs the HashSet model, models::BRINGS, and the result names both) and java.util.StringJoiner (add, toString; an empty join is the JDK's new String(), a gap, since the checker's builder gives the literal "" where the JDK's join makes a new String). Each is proved against its definition written out (claims.LinkedSets, claims.Joiners), sampled on a JVM, shows a left-out method still the JDK's call, and fails under mutation (no null after the elements, reversed order, no delimiter, "" for an empty join, "nul" for null). String.lastIndexOf(int) is modelled (claims.T#lastIndexOfPoint, and an evidence record whose ten boundary cases agree on the JVM, the interpreter and the checker), and Class.isArray() of a class literal (claims.Arrayed).

A fix found on the way: a Class method with a primitive result on a class the engine holds no literal of (isAssignableFrom, now isArray) was met under --gaps assume as an assumable reference gap that pushed no value, ending in 'operand stack underflow' with no verdict (never a false one). It is now a primitive gap, refused by name in both modes; the test fails with the old kind. The new tests run their JVMs with -XX:-UsePerfData after a parallel run printed an hsperfdata warning into the sampled output.

286's driver gives the protected-state tasks both new models; a capped probe still refutes 5.3.18 at trial bound 3. A capped probe with field restricted to someMap/SomeMap (not the frozen claim) now stops at PropertyAccessException.getLocalizedMessage() in DefaultBindingErrorProcessor.processPropertyAccessException:79: the exception's message and cause, which the JDK's exception constructors drop today. Verified: test_costs run --changed (26 of 26), validate_example 286, the mutations above. Job 20261117-192205 still has no result; ProtectedBeanStandIn.java is unchanged.

commits.summary: Example 286's someMap mismatch path runs to its end: a JDK exception keeps its message and cause, and the fixed task is proved over ASCII names in a probe (verification pending)
commits.body:
The binding error's default message is ex.getLocalizedMessage(), which Spring's NestedRuntimeException builds from Throwable's message and the cause's toString(). The own checker (lib/src/bmc/throwables.rs) now keeps a JDK exception's message and cause from its (), (String) and (String, Throwable) constructors. It models Throwable's getMessage, getCause, getLocalizedMessage (an application's getMessage runs in its place) and toString where they are Throwable's own, plus getClass() of a JDK exception and the builder's StringBuilder(int) and append(Object). The concatenation cap rose from 64 to 256 code units, since TypeMismatchException's message is about 150.

Two false proofs closed. A JDK exception's constructor is now exact only where its bytecode just passes its arguments up to Throwable's (JDK 25's flight-recorder hook allowed): UnknownFormatConversionException(null) throws on a JVM and is now a gap. An application's fillInStackTrace() override, which the JVM runs inside the constructor, is refused by name. With no JDK image, jdk_facts lists the plain constructors, and a unit test checks that list against the image's bytecode.

Verified: claims.Thrown (lib/tests/claims.rs) proves four statements a JVM confirms and leaves four a JVM breaks unverifiable by name. Each of five mutations makes a test fail. test_costs run --changed passes 23 of 23, and validate_example 286 passes. Capped probes: the fixed task (5.3.19) is proved at bound 7 with field restricted to someMap/SomeMap (113 s) and, through prove.py's new --assume-also trial, with field ASCII (108 s). Job 20261117-222610-example-286-s-fixed-protected-state-task runs the frozen claim at bound 8 (expected to stop only at non-ASCII toLowerCase()) and the ASCII trial at bound 8 (expected proved), each in a work folder apart from the accepted refutation's. Six capped probes of the preservation stream's rmvpqswzxlyv (step-6-probes.json): 307's preservation stops in 1 s at the previous revision's getBytes("UTF-8"), the mutant's at StandardCharsets.US_ASCII, and with the conversions modelled the claim's unwind 513 leaves no loop summarized, so nothing is tied and the check is killed at 4 GB in 39 s; at the default unwinding it ends at the time limit as 287 does.

lib/tests/fixtures/conversion-countermodels (twelve pairs, a prototype model as a patch, the test to add) and callee-countermodels (ten pairs for taking an unchanged callee as one function) each have a harness, check.py, and a README with what a JVM and today's checker say. commits.summary: Example 307: a prototype of the relation at the unchanged callee closes both tasks at crypt_raw on JDK 25, and the callee's code has no fingerprint there at hashpw(byte[], String)
commits.body:
A second delivery from the session the user brought in ahead of the preservation stream's step 6, for the stream to compare its own call-level rule against. New files, and edits to this session's own fixture; no checker source and no test changes.

examples/307-*/records/step-6-call-level.md is the note and step-6-call-level-probes.json the runs. lib/tests/fixtures/callee-countermodels/prototype-one-function.patch (against kskmpmny, git 10b5d9c0, after prototype-model.patch) names a callee's outcome by the key of the state at its entry, as a loop's state past the bound is named, and checks no side condition. With it, at the claim's frozen parameters and assumption, in capped probes (4 GB, 300 s): with the relation at crypt_raw on JDK 25, preservation is verified in 79 s (878 MB) and the mutant is a violation in 58 s, replayed on a JVM; with it at hashpw(byte[], String), preservation is verified in 53 s on JDK 21 and the run is killed at 4 GB on JDK 25, and the mutant has no verdict under the claim's seven salts (the first candidate has salt = null) and is a violation under one valid salt. Without a relation the runs die at 4 GB.

The JDK 25 difference: hashpw(byte[], String) calls Integer.parseInt, whose bytecode the checker follows, and JDK 25's parseInt(String, int) calls String.format(String, Object[]), which shared::reach takes as a way back into the application since kskmpmny. The fixture gains the row parsed (Parsing.java, a callee that calls Integer.parseInt): verified on JDK 21 and no verdict on JDK 25 on kskmpmny, in under a second.

The prototype against the fixture's rows: by formula it falsely proves wiped and counted (what the callee writes is not in its outcome); with a relation by content added it falsely proves table, seeded, helped and aliased too. No other row turns. So the rows separate a rule with its side conditions from one without.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the code two versions are taken to share past the reach's fix: an override removed, a hidden field, an interface's initializer two ways and the target's own class's, each taken as identical or tied where a JVM tells the versions apart
commits.body:
Item 5 of the challenge brief, against the preservation stream's kskmpmny (its fix for domain-advances-preservation-I010). The fix holds: built apart with the sources touched, tie_countermodels.rs passes there, its checker-side test included. Past it, lib/src/shared.rs's reach still leaves out five things, each shown by lib/tests/fixtures/reach-countermodels (old/ against new/), where each version alone gives 2 (0 for hidden) against 1 on a JVM (lib/tests/reach_countermodels.rs). Under the defaults, each of these is 'identical in both versions; nothing to prove' at kskmpmny and on this line alike, since the shortcut is older than the run: removed (an override the previous version declared and the new one inherits; only the new version's reach is walked and the old one is looked up by the new one's declaring class), hidden (a field the previous version declared that hides an inherited one; fields are not compared), constant (an interface's static read through an implementing class; the JVM initializes the interface, initialized() takes superclasses only), defaulted (making an object initializes a superinterface with a default method) and Own#f (the target's own class's initializer). looped, constant's read in a loop past the bound, is Verified under the ties at kskmpmny, non-vacuous; on this line it gets no verdict.

shared.rs is the preservation stream's this run, so nothing in lib/src changes here: the README's checker-side test, which fails on all six at kskmpmny, goes to it as a failure item citing this commit. Audit: the shortcut needs no --before-classpath, which 288 to 290 all pass; 289's rerun on kskmpmny unwinds fully; 287's BCrypt implements no interface and uses only its own fields in both pinned releases. A lemma's proof is a check of its own, given the check's stand-ins. The check that uses the lemma states the lemma as proved, and states only what its own run's engine noted. So at state's zlvqxmst, built apart, sn.Use#viaLemma is Verified through a lemma whose proof called a narrowly sampled stand-in, and its result names no stand-in; a JVM gives 32 where 0 is proved (lib/tests/fixtures/stand-in-countermodels). A model on request is lost the same way. Preservation's scan refuses athrow in a logged record's classes, but a JVM raises an Error without one: an OutOfMemoryError (new long[Integer.MAX_VALUE]) and a StackOverflowError (a recursion) in getMessage() each leave log through StreamHandler.publish's catch (Exception). Both are Verified 'log returned' at kskmpmny (lib/tests/fixtures/log-countermodels). The rules are those streams', so nothing in lib/src changes; each README has the checker-side test, which goes to the owner as a failure item. No accepted result rests on either: 286's simpleMatch lemma calls only String methods, and 287's LocationResolvingLogRecord neither recurses nor allocates by input.
